activities.caption: pair each agency with its gendered mechanism
activities.name: genAgenciesMatch

config.prompt: Pair each socialising agency with its mechanism:

pairs.right: assigns chores, tolerates roughness in boys and grades it in girls, talks more about feelings to daughters
the hidden curriculum — subject-encouragement gaps in maths and physics before age ten
the playground, where deviation gets its fastest sanctions
role stereotyping that persists in children's programming even as representation improves
children build 'what boys do / what girls do' and self-teach by selecting, imitating, remembering

config.why: The script is taught before anyone is born and rehearsed in every interaction afterwards — self-teaching through schemas, policed through accountability.

activities.anchor: applied with striking speed to deviation
activities.caption: find the faulty line — where control went
activities.name: genControlSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Teasing, exclusion, the raised eyebrow — the informal layer acts fast when a script is broken.
Dress codes and laws about who can drive, vote, own, inherit are the formal layer; most are now formally equal.
With formal equality largely won, control migrated entirely into the state's hands.
Hegemonic masculinity is a hierarchy among men, subordinating other masculinities.
Both scripts are structures, and both bill their bearers.
config.correction: Control migrated to the informal and institutional — the raised eyebrow replaced the statute as the main enforcement.
config.why: The feminine script prices compliance, appearance and care; the masculine one prices emotional restriction and risk.

config.why: Both are products of the same script — which is why 'what's in it for men' is a serious research and policy question.

activities.caption: drag between the interactional and the institutional
activities.name: genLevelsCompare

config.prompt: Drag between the interactional and the institutional level:

before.label: Interactional
before.text: the doing-gender machinery — in mixed-sex task groups men disproportionately claim airtime and credit even when equally informed; accountability renews the category in every encounter.

after.label: Institutional
after.text: workplaces designed around the two-carrier-family-with-a-housewife of the 1950s — full-time careers with no built-in caregiving; law, family-law defaults, benefit systems. The default worker is assumed child-free, mobile, backed by someone at home.

config.why: The three levels reinforce each other — and the default-worker assumption is where the economy meets the care economy.

config.hint: A feeling, an action, a pronoun, a year, a courtesy title.

config.prompt: ILO time-use data put women's share of the world's unpaid hours here — place it:
config.why: About three-quarters — roughly three times men's share; UN estimates value the work at 10–39% of GDP by country, often larger than manufacturing.

activities.anchor: The decomposition is more honest than that
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the pay-gap reading
activities.name: genDecompositionSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Control for occupation, hours and experience and the US residual shrinks to roughly 2-8%.
The biggest explained components are occupational segregation and reduced hours.
Those components are themselves gendered outcomes tracking the care assignment.
Once the controls are applied, the case for discrimination collapses.
Audit experiments — identical CVs, screened orchestras — find the unexplained residue directly.
config.correction: Controls tell you where the gap hides, not whether it is innocent.
config.why: The explained part is itself gendered — and the unexplained residue is found directly by experiment, not assumed away.
